Questions.question: Where was Imran when his mistake happened?
What caused Imran to damage the cutting bit?
Questions.answer: He tightened the tool post too quickly.
options: He increased the speed too much.
He tightened the tool post too quickly.

Questions.question: Where was Kavin during his mistake?
Why was Kavin’s surface cut uneven?
Questions.answer: He didn’t lock the workpiece firmly.
options: He didn’t lock the workpiece firmly.
He set the feed rate too high.

activity_b.text: Imran and Kavin walked up to Mr. Smith after the morning maintenance briefing.
Both looked uneasy, and Imran spoke first.
Good morning Sir, we need to talk to you.
We realised we made a few mistakes last week, and we want to explain them properly.
Good morning, both of you. Thank you for coming forward.
Let’s go through them one by one.
Now Imran, tell me what happened?
I damaged the cutting bit.
Where exactly were you when your problem occurred?
I was near the lathe machine, right beside the tool-storage rack.
And when did it happen? What time was it?
It was Wednesday, around ten fifteen, just before the precision-cutting session.
Alright. Now tell me—how did you end up damaging the cutting bit?
Sir… I tightened the tool post too quickly.
I should have adjusted the alignment first, but I didn’t.
I usually check the alignment, but not every single day—maybe two or three times a week.
And why didn’t you check it that morning?
Honestly, sir, I thought the setting was still correct from the last job.
But now I know I shouldn’t assume that.
Good. So how will you prevent this from happening again?
I’m going to check the alignment before starting work, tighten the tool post slowly, and record the settings in the logbook.
Alright. Now, Kavin, what was your mistake?
The surface cut in the milling task was uneven.
Where were you when your mistake happened?
I was near the milling machine, right beside the coolant-control panel.
And when was that?
Friday around 3.00 p.m., during the surface-milling task.
And how did your surface cut become so uneven?
Sir, I set the speed correctly, but I didn’t lock the workpiece firmly in the vice.
I also used the older cutter, and the edges weren’t sharp enough.
Why didn’t you check the cutter condition?
I was rushing, sir.
I check it most of the time, but that day I hurried because another job was waiting.
So how will you avoid these problems next time?
I’m going to secure the workpiece properly, use the newer cutter, and double-check the vice before starting.
I’ll also slow down when adjusting the feed rate.
Good. These are small mistakes—not failures—but they matter.
Let’s stay consistent this week.
